name: Jeffrey Epstein
lane: Core archive subject; banking; criminal/civil records
relationship: Central subject of the archive and account holder / principal in many source records.
sources: DOJ/court-filed Epstein records | GAH archive/search index
boundary: A central index subject; individual records must still be read for exact conduct, date, and evidentiary scope.

name: Ghislaine Maxwell
relationship: Named in federal court records and in source material connected to Epstein.
sources: United States v. Maxwell records | GAH archive/search index
boundary: Presence in an Epstein-connected source is not interchangeable with the specific conduct adjudicated in Maxwell’s criminal case.

name: JPMorgan Chase
relationship: Banked Epstein and later filed suspicious-activity reports that Senate Finance reconstructed.
sources: Senate Finance JPMorgan memorandum | JPMorgan litigation records | EFTA02810827
boundary: A SAR reports suspicious activity; it does not establish that every transaction was criminal.

name: Leon Black
lane: Financial relationship; advisory payments; later referrals
relationship: Paid Epstein for advisory work; public sources contain differing $158M and $170M aggregate totals.
sources: Dechert 2021 review | Senate Finance 2023–2026 records | USVI records
boundary: Large payments establish money movement and a financial relationship, not criminal purpose by themselves.

name: Apollo Global Management
relationship: Apollo’s Conflicts Committee commissioned the 2021 Dechert review of Black’s relationship with Epstein.
sources: SEC-filed Dechert review
boundary: The review context does not mean Apollo paid Epstein or participated in Epstein’s conduct.

name: Ehud Barak
relationship: Appears in a multi-year documentary record of scheduling, meetings, correspondence, and later business discussions involving Epstein.
sources: DOJ-released emails | Barak archive records | GAH source-map lane
boundary: Scheduling, introductions, and correspondence do not by themselves establish purpose, agency, intelligence activity, or wrongdoing.

name: Carbyne
relationship: Security-technology company discussed in the 2018–2019 Barak/Qatar correspondence chain.
sources: DOJ-released / archived correspondence
boundary: Discussion or a pitch does not establish a completed transaction, deployment, or government adoption.

name: Jabor Al Thani
relationship: Introduced by Epstein to Barak in the documented Qatar/Carbyne correspondence chain.
sources: Archived email chain
boundary: An introduction and follow-up correspondence do not establish agreement, procurement, or improper purpose.

name: Financial Trust Company, Inc.
relationship: Appears in bank statements and transaction records involving investments and the 2012 Black Family Partners asset sale.
sources: Financial Trust bank records | SEC records | GAH transaction reconstruction
boundary: Ownership or investment activity does not by itself establish operational control or downstream conduct.

name: Black Family Partners, L.P.
relationship: Counterparty in the documented November 2012 purchase of Financial Trust assets, including ESWW-related interests.
sources: 2012 sale-package records | Financial Trust bank receipt
boundary: The transaction record establishes the sale and receipt; it does not, by itself, identify the ultimate source of every dollar used for the purchase.

name: Environmental Solutions Worldwide (ESWW)
relationship: Public-company investment held by Financial Trust and later included in the 2012 Black Family Partners transaction.
sources: SEC filings | Financial Trust schedules | GAH transaction reconstruction
boundary: Investment and share ownership do not establish operational control or causation for later government use of the company’s technology.

name: Jes Staley
relationship: Appears in JPMorgan records and later litigation concerning the bank’s relationship with Epstein.
sources: JPMorgan litigation records | Senate Finance reconstruction
boundary: A banker-client relationship and internal references must be separated from any specific knowledge or conduct claim.

name: Jorge Amador
relationship: Forensic accountant whose June 16, 2023 expert report analyzed Epstein-related JPMorgan accounts and transaction patterns.
boundary: His characterizations of suspiciousness and legitimate business purpose are expert opinions, not judicial findings.

name: Darren Indyke
relationship: Appears in Epstein-related legal and financial execution records and later transaction reviews.
sources: GAH source-locked financial/legal records | Senate/Treasury references where cited
boundary: Record presence and execution of transactions do not establish knowledge of unrelated criminal conduct.

name: Alexander Acosta
relationship: U.S. Attorney whose office negotiated and approved the 2007 non-prosecution agreement; OPR later reviewed the decision.
sources: DOJ OPR report | 2007 privilege log / term sheet records
boundary: OPR found poor judgment but did not find professional misconduct or evidence of a corrupt or impermissible motive.

name: A. Marie Villafaña
relationship: Lead prosecutor whose emails and later statement anchor key prosecution and victim-notification chronology.
sources: EFTA00013764 | EFTA00225044 | DOJ OPR report
boundary: Her later statement is retrospective and should be distinguished from contemporaneous records.

name: Jeffrey Sloman
relationship: First Assistant U.S. Attorney who sent the December 7, 2007 “Hold the letter” instruction.
sources: EFTA00013764 | DOJ OPR interview record
boundary: The native email establishes the hold instruction; it does not identify the person Sloman later recalled speaking to.

name: DOJ Office of Professional Responsibility
relationship: Conducted the official review of the 2006–2008 federal Epstein investigation and NPA process.
sources: DOJ OPR full report | DOJ public findings
boundary: OPR is a retrospective official review; its findings do not substitute for the underlying primary records where those records are available.

name: Metropolitan Correctional Center, New York
relationship: Federal detention facility where Epstein was held and died in August 2019.
sources: DOJ OIG Report 23-085 | SDNY Noel/Thomas case
boundary: Documented custodial failures do not, by themselves, establish third-party criminality in the death.

name: Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands
relationship: Brought civil litigation involving Epstein-related banking activity and entered a 2023 settlement with Leon Black.
sources: USVI litigation records | USVI government financial statements
boundary: Civil allegations and settlements must be kept separate from criminal findings and admissions.
